diagnosis.rootCause: Every world-space label (villager plates, ! and ? markers, speech bubbles, landmark names, enemy plates, Mira) was drawn straight at its projected point. Nothing checked the HUD panels, the screen edges, line of sight or other labels. The only guard was an enemy-only rule, y < 140 || y > 560. Four specific causes: (1) Speech bubbles used a fixed offset from the head (vp.y - 50 - bh) that sits right on the marker rect (vp.y - 88 to vp.y - 40), so Sefa Brine's bubble hid his '!'. Bubbles also had no HUD or overlap checks, so they could cover the tracker and other people's nameplates. (2) Landmark names had no HUD or top-edge check, so 'Pilgrims' Rest' and 'Carrion Cliffs' drew over Mira's frame and 'Pilgrims' Rest' was clipped at the top edge. (3) There was no occlusion test and no overlap handling, so plates showed through walls and stacked into one another. (4) Enemy plates were fixed at root + 1.7 m, tuned for humanoids. A boar's back is at about root - 0.2 m and a wolf's at about root + 0.1 m, and seen from close up that gap is 150 to 250 px, so the plates floated well above the beasts. Separately, the 13 px resource bar drew its '100 Vigor' label in a 13 px rect, which clipped it (the label style's padding left about 10 px for a 12 px bold font). The tracker's 'no quests tracked' block (zone name plus 'Look for gold ! ...') never timed out, so it sat over the scene for good. The fix rebuilds the world-label pass in EncounterHud.cs, which runs on Repaint only. Plates are gathered, sorted nearest-first and placed with Place(): nudged inside the screen, lifted past labels already placed, and hidden if they would cover a HUD rect or go off the top. The HUD rects are the player, party and target frames, the minimap, the tracker's real extent from the last frame, chat, and the bottom bars. Line of sight uses one Physics.RaycastNonAlloc per label from the camera to the head. It ignores colliders under an Actor or a TreeFade and triggers; landmark labels ignore anything within 8 m in front of the label point. Bubbles are placed last, above the plate and marker box, so they can never cover a marker. When a HUD panel blocks one, it slides sideways off the panel or is hidden, and it fades over its last half second. Enemy plates sit 0.45 m above each model's real top, measured once from its renderer bounds and capped at 1.7 x scale, so beasts get low plates. Label strings and the measuring GUIContent are cached, so the loops don't allocate each frame. DrawHeadMarker is split into HeadMarker() (which marker) and DrawHeadMarker(char, grey, at) (draw it where the stack ended up). UnitBar gives thin bars an 18 px label rect centred on the bar. The empty-tracker hint fades 20 s after you arrive in a zone or after the last tracked quest ends. DrawQuests also records trackerArea for the label pass.

edits.why: Rewrites the world-label pass (nameplates, ! and ? markers, speech bubbles, place names). Labels stay out of HUD panels and inside the screen. One ray each (ignoring actors and trees) hides them behind solid scenery. Overlapping plates stack nearest-first. Bubbles go above the whole plate-and-marker stack, so they never cover a quest marker. Enemy plates sit at each model's real height, low for beasts. The pass runs only on Repaint, and the old per-villager GUIStyle, per-enemy label string and per-target edge-array allocations are gone. Fixes items 1-5 (oakhaven-97/98/99, khaven-98/99, peaks-97/98, ashrim-97/98).

If that agent changes those exact lines (for example a tracker backing panel), re-anchor. A tracker backing panel should also fade with the hint, or the panel will be left empty once the hint is gone.

Policy is to hide, not fade: a plate, marker or place name that would touch a HUD panel is not drawn. For example, a quest giver standing just under the target frame loses its plate while something is targeted. Bubbles first try sliding sideways off the panel.

Line of sight uses colliders. Building 'Solid' boxes can be larger than the visible mesh near roofs, and invisible colliders (zone boundary walls, the Wasting boundary) also block sight. The ray skips colliders under an Actor or a TreeFade and all triggers. Orchard trees have no TreeFade, but their 0.3 m trunks rarely matter. A targeted enemy out of sight also loses its plate; the ground ring still marks it.

An enemy's plate height is measured once, the first time it is drawn standing, from its enabled renderers' bounds. Result: top + 0.45 m, capped at 1.7 x lossyScale.y. A weapon raised mid-swing at that moment could add about 0.1 m. Enemies that were already dead when loaded keep the 1.7 m default. Dead enemies still show plates, as before.

Place names ignore anything within 8 m in front of the label point. That keeps a landmark's own building (the Great Oak trunk, the inn) from hiding its name, but a wall closer than that to the label point won't hide it either.

diagnosis.rootCause:
The free-floating HUD text has no backing and at most a weak shadow. (1)/(2) The quest tracker in DrawQuests, and the legacy DrawQuestTracker, draws tan text straight onto the scene using Shadow(), which offsets one black copy by 1px. That is too thin over bright grass, sky and walls. When nothing is tracked, the same block shows the zone name and the "Look for gold !" hint forever, with no backing and no time-out. (3) DrawChat always fills a fixed 470x150 black .32 rectangle at (10,620), however few messages there are, so it reads as an empty box, worst at night. (4) Enemy nameplates in DrawWorldLabels are drawn with a bare GUI.Label (no shadow or outline) in con colours. Yellow "Even" text vanishes on yellow-green grass, and the label is left-aligned at x-90, so it sits off-centre from its x-65..x+65 health bar. Mira's plate also has no shadow at all.

Fix: add two small helpers. Outlined() draws a 1px outline from 4 diagonal dark copies, painted on Repaint only. HudBacking() draws an ink plate at .5 alpha with a faint gold top rule, matching the action bar's ink and gold style.
- Tracker: the plate is sized to the previous pass's measured text extent. IMGUI paints in call order, so the plate must be drawn before the text; the one-pass lag is invisible.
- Hint: when nothing is tracked, the zone name and hint show for 14 s on zone entry, or after the last tracked quest ends, then fade over 2 s.
- Chat: the plate hugs the drawn lines, stays for 8 s after the last message, fades over 3 s, and comes back while the mouse hovers the log. The text stays, outlined.
- Nameplates: outlined and centred over their bar, with a cached style. Mira and villager plates use the same outline.
- Measuring reuses one GUIContent, which removes the per-line `new GUIContent` in the tracker and chat.

If so, those three oldStrings (edits 5-7) will not match. They are independent of the others and can be dropped or re-applied on top of that cluster's version with the same Outlined(...) call.

If the other cluster adds members with the same names (Outlined, HudBacking, measureContent, enemyPlateStyle, trackerW/H/X, chatTop/chatW/chatAt, TrackerBegin, TrackLine, HintSeconds, ChatArea), the build fails with duplicate-member errors. None of these exist in the current sources.
The plate uses the previous IMGUI pass's measured size, so on the first frame after a change it is one pass stale. This is invisible in practice.

By design the zone hint and zone title disappear 14 s after arriving in a zone with nothing tracked. They return on the next zone change or when the last tracked quest ends. Captures taken more than 14 s after load in ashrim or peaks will show no tracker block.

The chat plate fades to nothing when idle, while the message text stays with an outline. Hovering over (10,620,470,150) brings the plate back. New messages are detected in the HUD by count plus first/last string reference; a literal string repeated six times in a row would not re-show the plate (harmless).

Outlined text costs five labels per line, but the four outline copies are painted only on Repaint. That is roughly 100 extra labels per repaint with a full tracker, full chat and several nameplates, which is acceptable for IMGUI.

review.notes:
The patch is sound as proposed, so no corrected edits are needed. I checked it without running Unity.

**What I checked**
- **Edits apply:** Every one of the 14 oldStrings appears exactly once in the current working-tree files. The files use LF line endings, and the special characters (✓, –, ◆) match. I applied all 14 to fresh copies in scratchpad\review. The result is byte-identical to the proposer's patched files in scratchpad\hud, and those match the JSON edits.
- **Compile:** I recompiled all runtime sources with Unity's own compiler, against the Unity module DLLs and netstandard 2.1. It succeeds with 0 errors. The only warning, CS0169 for the unused field bookScroll, was already there before the patch. None of the new member names exist anywhere under Assets/Crulanda. session.ZoneId, session.Messages and QuestState.tracked all exist.
- **IMGUI behaviour:**
  - GUI.Label reserves no control ID and only draws on Repaint, so drawing the outline copies on Repaint only cannot break other controls.
  - Mouse position is in 1440x900 canvas space, so the chat hover check works.
  - CalcSize ignores word wrap, and the patch clamps to the line's right edge, so wrapped lines get the full tracker width.
  - Because the Layout pass runs before Repaint in the same frame, the plate is not actually one frame behind.
  - session.Message caps the log at 6 lines, so a new message always changes the count or the first/last line, and the plate reappears.
- **Layout on the 1440x900 canvas:**
  - The tracker plate covers x 1112 to at most 1438 and starts at y 236, below the minimap's +/- buttons (y ≤ 233). It stays inside the existing tracker click-blocking area (1110,236,330,200).
  - The chat plate is never wider than the old 470 box and still ends at y 770. The key-help line at y 774 is unchanged.
  - The enemy name is now centred on x, over its bar (x-65..x+65). Its 22px-high box (y-24..y-2) sits inside the target box (y-25..y+13).
  - Mira and villager plates keep the distance fade, because the outline alpha follows the text colour.
- **Against the shots:**
  - Tracker on oakhaven 97/98/99: dark plate plus outline.
  - Zone hint on ashrim 97/98 and peaks 97: plate plus outline, then gone after 12 s plus a 2 s fade.
  - Chat on oakhaven-99-pond-night and peaks-97: the plate fits the lines and fades 8–11 s after the last message.
  - Yellow "2 Grey wolf" on grass (oakhaven-99-ambush-sprung): outlined and centred. It was left-aligned at x-90, off-centre from its bar, as the shot shows.
- **Garbage per frame:** The patch removes the per-line `new GUIContent` in the tracker and chat, and caches the enemy name style. The new work allocates nothing: only value types and a foreach over a List of tuples.
- **Tests:** Nothing under Tests/ references EncounterHud or HUD state; the only "Messages" hit is an unrelated test in LogTests.cs.

**Non-blocking points for the orchestrator**
1. Existing garbage, outside this patch: the villager loop still makes a `new GUIStyle(small)` per villager every frame (EncounterHud.cs line 401). The action bar also makes new GUIStyles per slot, and the target box builds a new Rect[] each frame. The villager style is worth caching, but it was deliberately left alone because the other nameplate cluster may rewrite that code.
2. Existing layering: world labels are drawn before the tracker. Any "!" marker or speech bubble that lands in the tracker area now sits under the 50% ink plate. That is fine for a HUD over the world.
3. Retakes: the capture script's 97–99 shots come after long sequences of other captures. Retakes of ashrim/peaks will show no hint unless they are taken within about 12 s of arriving in the zone. That is intended; the verify steps already say so.
4. Merge order: as the proposer notes, the enemy name, Mira and villager edits (5–7) will not match if the nameplate/occlusion cluster lands first. Re-apply them as the same `Outlined(...)` calls on top of that version.
